cards.explanation: The answer is that the LORD stirred Cyrus to fulfill His word spoken through Jeremiah. Ezra 1:1 says the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus, king of Persia, "…to fulfill the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah…" The LORD had said it, and now He was making it happen. Then Cyrus puts a proclamation in writing for his whole kingdom. That's a king who doesn't lose the memo.

The answer is house. Cyrus says the LORD, the God of heaven, "…has appointed me to build a house for Him at Jerusalem in Judah." (Ezra 1:2). Cyrus, king of Persia, is the one saying it. A king with a whole kingdom to run, and he's announcing a house for the LORD, in writing, no less.

The answer is False. Cyrus says, "The LORD, the God of heaven, who has given me all the kingdoms of the earth…" (Ezra 1:2). He credits the LORD, not his armies. A king handing the credit to someone else, friends, I don't see that every day.

The answer is that his God will be with him. Cyrus says, "…may his God be with him, and may he go to Jerusalem in Judah…" (Ezra 1:3). The wish is that God be with each one who goes. Cyrus is the king of Persia, and he's wishing it for people who belong to the LORD.

The answer is True. Cyrus says, "…let every survivor, wherever he lives, be assisted by the men of that region with silver, gold, goods, and livestock…" (Ezra 1:4). That's a lot of help for one trip. A freewill offering for the house of God goes along with it too.

The answer is True. Ezra 1:5 says the family heads of Judah and Benjamin, the priests and the Levites, "…everyone whose spirit God had stirred…" prepared to go. The same God who stirred the king also stirred them. I think that's a nice thing to notice.

The answer is the articles from the house of the LORD. Ezra 1:7 says Cyrus "…brought out the articles belonging to the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem…" Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon. Those articles were headed back to where they belonged.
The answer is True. Ezra 1:7 says Nebuchadnezzar had carried the articles away from Jerusalem and "…placed in the temple of his gods." Now King Cyrus is bringing them out.

The answer is Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah. Ezra 1:8 says Mithredath the treasurer "…counted them out to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah." Verse 11 says Sheshbazzar brought all these along when the exiles went up from Babylon to Jerusalem. That's 5,400 articles, friends, and I'd want that man on inventory day.

The answer is that they are kept out of the priesthood. Ezra 2:62 says these men searched for their family records, couldn't find them, and "…so were excluded from the priesthood as unclean." Records mattered for priests. I think this one hurts.

The answer is True. Ezra 2:63 says, "The governor ordered them not to eat the most holy things until there was a priest to consult the Urim and Thummim." So the matter waits until there's a priest to consult them.

The answer is some of the heads of the families. Ezra 2:68 says, "…some of the heads of the families gave freewill offerings to rebuild the house of God on its original site." Some of the heads of the families, that's who the verse names. Not every family, and not only the priests and Levites.
The answer is False. Ezra 2:68 says the family heads gave "…to rebuild the house of God on its original site." So the plan was to put it back where it stood, not to start over somewhere new.

The answer is as much as each is able. Ezra 2:69 says, "According to their ability, they gave to the treasury for this work…" Each gave what he could. The verse lists 61,000 darics of gold, 5,000 minas of silver and 100 priestly garments.
